video_title: Bitcoin, Gold and Anthropic: Where the Money Goes Next
gist: Granite Shares CEO Will Rind discusses the ~$80B Anthropic IPO as the first public pure-play frontier AI lab (and his firm's AIL/ANS 2x long/short ETFs on it), expecting SpaceX-like volatility amid AI skepticism. He argues gold and Bitcoin have lagged as capital rotated to AI but remain supported long-term by government debt and debasement, and explains how GLD became the blueprint for Bitcoin ETFs and why ETF economics favor scale players.

themes.theme: Anthropic IPO: pure-play frontier lab exposure and volatility setup

insights.claim: Anthropic's IPO is raising about $80 billion, described as the largest IPO in history and likely the biggest from a retail-participation perspective, surpassing SpaceX.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano / Will Rind
insights.so_what: Retail-heavy mega-IPO implies outsized post-listing flows and volatility; size the position for swings.
insights.quote: Anthropic is going public. They're raising$80 billion dollars. It's the largest IPO in history.

insights.claim: Will Rind argues the dominant investor view is that Anthropic is the first listed pure-play frontier AI lab, whereas all prior public AI exposure has been adjacencies such as semiconductors, chips and power.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Expect a scarcity premium for pure-play AI-lab exposure; this may pull capital from AI-adjacent names into Anthropic.
insights.quote: there's not really been that pure play exposure to the frontier lab that has the pure intelligence core business model

insights.claim: Rind expects Anthropic's post-IPO trading to be volatile like SpaceX's (which listed around $125-135, spiked over $200, fell to ~$100 and settled ~$130-140), but in a more skeptical mood than SpaceX's euphoric debut at the peak of the semiconductor rally.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Use the SpaceX round-trip as a template: an early pop followed by a deep retrace is plausible; avoid chasing day-one strength.
insights.quote: When SpaceX came to market you know there was euphoria in the market. I mean it was pretty much the peak of the semiconductor uh rally

insights.claim: The Anthropic IPO is reported as oversubscribed and has given the broader AI trade a short-term 'shot in the arm' after weeks of AI-bubble skepticism.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Watch whether IPO-driven sentiment sustains AI-complex strength or fades like the post-SpaceX period.

insights.claim: The bear case on Anthropic centers on broad AI-bubble skepticism, a significant drawdown in semis, Nvidia's recent leadership-related 'debacle', and concerns about the sustainability of Anthropic's business model and the post-midterms battle over data centers.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Key risks to monitor: business-model sustainability and data-center policy fights; these could cap Anthropic's valuation.
insights.quote: people have some real concerns about how sustainable that's going to be and the battle especially since the midterms the battle for data centers

insights.claim: Anthropic faces competition from closed-source US labs (SpaceX's AI unit, Google, OpenAI) and open-source models including Chinese models, and its listing may influence OpenAI's own IPO aspirations.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano / Will Rind
insights.so_what: Anthropic's IPO reception is a read-through for an eventual OpenAI listing and for private AI-lab valuations.

insights.claim: Macro is a headwind versus the SpaceX IPO period: interest rates and inflation are higher now, which can weigh on high-multiple AI listings.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Higher rates pressure long-duration growth valuations; Anthropic's trading is sensitive to rate moves.
insights.quote: interest rates are higher, inflation's higher. So there are lots of forces that can act as a headwind

themes.theme: Leveraged single-stock ETFs on IPOs (Granite Shares playbook)

insights.claim: Granite Shares is launching 2x leveraged single-stock ETFs on Anthropic: AIL (2x long) and ANS (2x short), explicitly intended for traders and sophisticated investors rather than long-term holders.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: AIL/ANS flows can serve as a retail-sentiment gauge on Anthropic; leverage decay makes them unsuitable as buy-and-hold.
insights.quote: they're for traders. I mean, clearly anytime you use leverage, you've got heightened level of risk.

insights.claim: Granite Shares previously launched leveraged products around the SpaceX IPO (SPAL 2x long, SNK 2x short) and on SK Hynix, and Anthropic is its third IPO-linked launch, building a repeatable playbook of fast leveraged wrappers on hot listings.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Expect leveraged single-stock ETFs to appear quickly around every mega-IPO, amplifying early volatility.

insights.claim: Granite Shares claims to have pioneered leveraged single-stock products in the UK in 2019 and launched the first such US products in 2022.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: First-mover brand recognition matters in the leveraged single-stock niche where small issuers compete.

insights.claim: Ticker memorability is a core competitive weapon for ETF issuers; tickers are obtained from the exchange, and exchanges have cracked down on reserving them as US tickers (letters only) become scarce 'prime real estate', unlike Europe where numbers can denote leverage.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Ticker scarcity raises barriers for new entrants; memorable tickers can drive retail flows independent of product quality.
insights.quote: we're running out of tickers and so it's become, you know, like prime real estate

themes.theme: Gold and Bitcoin: debt debasement thesis vs. AI capital rotation

insights.claim: Gold and Bitcoin have suffered as capital has been sucked into the AI trade, according to the host's framing, which Rind does not dispute.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano
insights.so_what: Hard-asset weakness may be a flow/rotation story rather than a broken thesis; watch for reversal if AI enthusiasm cools.

insights.claim: Gold's deep selloff after a massive run-up is linked to rates rising rather than falling despite the Fed regime change, plus persistent inflation and higher energy and commodity prices.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Gold's near-term direction hinges on real rates; a turn in rates could restart the rally.
insights.quote: We've had the regime change at the Fed, but interest rates have not gone down. They've gone up.

insights.claim: Central bank gold buying remains the biggest and still very strong source of gold demand.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Structural central-bank bid supports gold on dips even when macro flows are negative.

insights.claim: Rind's core long-term case for gold and Bitcoin is that governments, especially in the West, have few options to handle debt other than inflating it away, debasing currencies, and he sees no political will to change this.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Maintain a hard-asset allocation as a hedge against fiscal dominance and currency debasement.
insights.quote: It doesn't seem like we've got the political will to change that in any meaningful way.

insights.claim: The 'productive assets beat non-productive assets' rule from economics 101 has not held over 5-25 years because gold and Bitcoin have done very well versus stocks; Rind says it would hold only with balanced budgets, controlled debt and real GDP growth.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano / Will Rind
insights.so_what: Investors should update allocation frameworks for a high-debt regime where hard assets compete with equities.

insights.claim: Rind is skeptical of Elon Musk's argument that AI will be so deflationary governments must print more money, saying it is too early to see evidence, and favors the bigger-government, higher-spending, higher-tax trend as bullish for gold.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Don't bank on AI-driven deflation yet; fiscal expansion remains the dominant driver for gold.

themes.theme: Nvidia: strong fundamentals vs. priced-in expectations

insights.claim: Nvidia reported strong earnings and is guiding roughly 75% year-over-year growth as a $4+ trillion company, yet the stock has been weighed down by controversy around Jensen Huang.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano / Will Rind
insights.so_what: Fundamentals remain strong; headline/key-person risk, not demand, is driving the discount.

insights.claim: Rind says Nvidia beat-and-raise quarters sometimes haven't been enough because results are priced in, but the latest results act as a catalyst showing the business is intact and there is 'life after Jensen'.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Price reaction to beats is a sentiment gauge; a business intact post-leadership change de-risks the name.

insights.claim: Rind frames the Anthropic and Nvidia bull/bear debate as entirely a function of one's belief in AI as the most profound technological change of our lifetimes.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Position sizing in AI names should reflect conviction in the secular thesis, not quarterly noise.

themes.theme: ETF wrappers unlocking asset classes: GLD to Bitcoin ETFs

insights.claim: GLD launched in 2004 as an initiative of the World Gold Council, a trade body owned by the largest gold miners seeking to increase gold demand, and it became the largest gold ETF and largest commodity fund in the world.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Producers creating access vehicles to boost demand is a recurring pattern to watch in other assets.

insights.claim: A first-to-market ETF that unlocks an asset class in brokerage portfolios creates a demand surge and a network effect of options, leveraged and derivative products that deepens liquidity and visibility.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Look for asset classes not yet in a 'marquee ETF' wrapper as candidates for demand step-changes.
insights.quote: the best solutions in life are when you provide a solution to a real problem.

insights.claim: GLD was the blueprint for US Bitcoin ETFs, which unlocked advisory demand because advisers charging around 1% can get paid on Bitcoin held in client portfolios; BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF is reportedly its most profitable fund.
insights.speaker: Anthony Pompliano / Will Rind
insights.so_what: Adviser-channel economics are a durable structural source of Bitcoin demand.
insights.quote: gold and GLD was the blueprint that was used for the launch of Bitcoin ETFs

insights.claim: ETF pricing power is inverted versus most industries: scale players like BlackRock, State Street and Vanguard win on price, so smaller issuers must compete on innovation such as leveraged ETFs or options-based income.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Expect continued proliferation of niche/complex ETFs from small issuers; commoditized categories consolidate to giants.
insights.quote: In ETF world or in financial services it's the opposite. It's completely inverted.

themes.theme: Global ETF markets: US scale, Asian retail vigor, European stagnation

insights.claim: The US ETF market benefits from one market, one exchange system, one regulator, one currency and one language, while Europe's fragmentation across countries, exchanges, regulators and languages raises costs and splits liquidity.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Structural cost advantages favor US-listed products and issuers.

insights.claim: European retail investors are smaller, more conservative and risk-averse, which Rind attributes to financial literacy, whereas Korea, Japan and Taiwan have vibrant growing economies generating excess wealth and active retail investing; Granite Shares often has a top-10 product at brokerages in Korea and Japan.
insights.speaker: Will Rind
insights.so_what: Asian retail flows are a key demand source for leveraged products; Europe's weak investing culture mirrors its lack of IPOs and major tech companies.
